title: India passes one crore HPV vaccine doses; six states cover every eligible girl
dek: About 87% of the year's 1.2 crore 14-year-old girls have had the single-dose vaccine against cervical cancer, the Health Ministry said. Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Odisha trail.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India has given more than one crore doses of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine to 14-year-old girls in less than nine months, the Union Health Ministry said on Saturday, covering about 87% of the year's target group in a national campaign against cervical cancer.

The target cohort is about 1.2 crore girls, estimated from the Registrar General of India's 2021 population projections, according to the ministry's figures. Six states have vaccinated all the girls in their target group: Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar.

## Where states stand

Uttar Pradesh has vaccinated the largest number of girls, more than 29 lakh, followed by Bihar with more than 13 lakh and Gujarat with nearly 8 lakh, according to the ministry. Assam has covered more than 95% of its target group, Telangana just over 95%, and Karnataka and Uttarakhand more than 90%.

Several large states are further behind. Reported coverage stands at about 86% in Chhattisgarh, 85% in Rajasthan, 77% in Kerala, 76% in Tamil Nadu and 75% in Odisha, according to reports. The figures released on Saturday, as reported, did not include West Bengal.

Health Minister J P Nadda congratulated the states and said the progress "reflects the collective commitment of States and Union Territories". He said India was "moving closer to a future free from cervical cancer".

## How the campaign works

The vaccine is given free, as a single dose, at government health facilities. Vaccination is voluntary. Each dose is recorded on U-WIN, the government's digital vaccination platform, which tracks beneficiaries and issues digital records.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the campaign at Ajmer in Rajasthan on 28 February 2026. Its pace has been steady: the ministry reported nearly 50 lakh doses in June and more than 80 lakh in September.

## Why it matters

Cervical cancer is one of the most common cancers among Indian women, and almost all cases are caused by long-lasting infection with high-risk types of HPV. Vaccinating girls before they are exposed to the virus is the main way to prevent it, which is why the campaign targets 14-year-olds. The World Health Organization recommends that countries vaccinate 90% of girls by age 15 as part of its strategy to eliminate cervical cancer as a public health problem.

The single-dose schedule, which the WHO has endorsed since 2022, makes a campaign of this scale cheaper and simpler to run than the earlier two- or three-dose regimens.

## What happens next

The campaign is an annual programme: each year a new group of girls turns 14 and becomes eligible. The ministry has not said when it expects the remaining states to reach full coverage of this year's group. Screening of adult women, which detects pre-cancerous changes early, remains the main protection for women who are too old to benefit from the vaccine.
